_comment: PER-MODEL LIST PRICES, USD per 1,000,000 tokens.
THIS FILE IS A MEASUREMENT WITH AN EXPIRY, not a constant. A price that has
moved does not fail: it silently produces a wrong dollar figure, in a report
whose whole purpose is to be quoted at somebody deciding whether to fund an
ingestion programme. So every estimate this table feeds is stamped with
`measured` and with `source`, and estimate-cost.mjs REFUSES to run when the
table is older than `stale_after_days` unless the caller passes
--accept-stale-prices. Loudness is the whole design: the failure mode of a
stale price is a confident wrong number, and the only defence against a
silent wrong answer is to make it noisy.
WHERE THESE CAME FROM: the `claude-api` skill's Current Models table, itself
cached at the date below. The live source is the pricing page named in
`source`; re-read it and update `measured` in the same edit. Do not update
one without the other.
CACHING IS MODELLED, because on this pipeline it is the dominant real-world
discount and ignoring it would overstate every figure: one statute is re-read
across many turns. The two multipliers below are DOCUMENTED APPROXIMATIONS
(read ~0.1x input, write ~1.25x input) and are applied only to cache tokens a
ledger actually measured. Per-model cache rates exist and differ; when one
matters, add it to that model's entry as `cache_read` and it wins over the
multiplier.
WHAT IS NOT MODELLED, on purpose, because each would make the estimate look
more precise than it is:
- batch processing, which is 50% off and applies to nothing the pipeline
currently does interactively.
- effort level, which changes output tokens by a large factor and is a
property of how a stage is invoked rather than of the model.
- partner platforms (Bedrock, Vertex), which are separately priced.
These exclusions are printed with every estimate rather than kept here.
